SMTC.title: Guidance was raised, not cut: the drop came from the 2030 targets
text: At its Data Center Analyst Day on 15 October, Semtech raised its outlook for the quarter to January (fiscal Q3 2027): sales $417.5m ± $2.5m (was $410m ± $5m), adjusted EPS $1.14 ± $0.02 (was $1.05 ± $0.03), adjusted operating margin 33.0% (was 31.0%).

What disappointed was the fiscal 2030 framework, which the company calls targets, not guidance: sales of $3.2bn (data center $2.1bn), adjusted EPS of $12.40–13.00, 70% gross margin and 48–50% operating margin. Investors had priced in more, and the stock fell 10% that day and about 24% over the week, after Northland's valuation downgrade on 9 October and an AI-hardware selloff on 12 October.

Analysts raised their numbers afterwards: next fiscal year's consensus EPS (FY2028) went from $5.86 a week earlier to $6.67. Stifel cut its price target to $200 and Northland turned positive again. At $136 the stock trades at about 11× the midpoint of the 2030 EPS target.
